Generate a 3D model of an octopus chef at a ramen booth

Make it in Blender, working in the current directory.
- A Blender 5 instance is running for you with no window (background mode). Use it through the `blender`
  MCP tools: run Python (`bpy`) with execute_blender_code, and look things up with the API and manual
  search tools. Blender's working directory is the current directory. The scene starts as Blender's
  default one (a cube, a camera and a light).
- There is no window to screenshot. To check your work, render it to an image file and look at the image
  (render_thumbnail_to_path, render_viewport_to_path, or a render of the scene camera to a file).
  Keep renders quick: a single tool call may take at most 5 minutes.
- Build it in Blender itself; don't write the model or the images any other way.
- Save the finished result in ./output/ (only what is in ./output/ is published):
  - the model or scene as one .glb file (glTF binary), shown on the site in an interactive 3D viewer:
    `bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(filepath=..., export_format='GLB')`, without Draco or meshopt
    compression, at most 15 MB;
  - one or more final renders as .png or .jpg, at most 2 MB each, from camera angles you choose.
  At most 8 files in all.
- Tools available on this machine: python3 3.15.0 (standard library only), node 26.12.0 (no npm packages), ffmpeg 9.0.2, ffprobe 9.0.2. Don't install packages or download anything (no asset
  libraries or add-ons).
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory.
- Finish with a short summary of what you made.
Building your octopus chef and ramen booth in Blender.

import bpy, math
# Clear
bpy.ops.object.select_all(action='SELECT')
bpy.ops.object.delete()

def mat(name, color):
    m=bpy.data.materials.new(name)
    m.use_nodes=True
    bsdf=m.node_tree.nodes["Principled BSDF"]
    bsdf.inputs["Base Color"].default_value=(*color,1)
    return m

red=mat("Octo",(0.85,0.25,0.3))
white=mat("White",(0.95,0.95,0.95))
black=mat("Black",(0.05,0.05,0.05))
wood=mat("Wood",(0.55,0.32,0.15))
darkwood=mat("DarkWood",(0.35,0.2,0.1))
cream=mat("Cream",(0.95,0.88,0.75))
broth=mat("Broth",(0.85,0.55,0.2))
green=mat("Green",(0.2,0.6,0.3))
roofm=mat("Roof",(0.6,0.15,0.12))
hatm=mat("Hat",(0.97,0.97,0.97))

def prim_mesh(name, loc, scale, material, primitive):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(location=loc) if primitive=='cube' else None
    o=bpy.context.active_object
    o.name=name
    o.scale=scale
    o.data.materials.append(material)
    return o

def add_uvsphere(name,loc,r,material,scale=(1,1,1)):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_uv_sphere_add(location=loc,radius=r)
    o=bpy.context.active_object; o.name=name
    o.scale=scale
    o.data.materials.append(material)
    return o
def add_cyl(name,loc,r,depth,material,scale=(1,1,1)):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(location=loc,radius=r,depth=depth)
    o=bpy.context.active_object; o.name=name
    o.scale=scale
    o.data.materials.append(material)
    return o
def add_torus(name,loc,maj,minr,material):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_torus_add(location=loc,major_radius=maj,minor_radius=minr)
    o=bpy.context.active_object; o.name=name
    o.data.materials.append(material)
    return o
def add_cone(name,loc,r1,depth,material):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cone_add(location=loc,radius1=r1,depth=depth)
    o=bpy.context.active_object; o.name=name
    o.data.materials.append(material)
    return o

# Octopus body
body=add_uvsphere("Body",(0,0,1.6),0.7,red,scale=(1,1,1.15))
# eyes
for x in (-0.25,0.25):
    add_uvsphere(f"EyeW{x}",(x,0.55,1.85),0.16,white)
    add_uvsphere(f"Pupil{x}",(x,0.68,1.85),0.07,black)
# chef hat
add_cyl("HatBase",(0,0,2.55),0.38,0.25,hatm)
add_uvsphere("HatTop",(0,0,2.85),0.45,hatm,scale=(1,1,0.7))
# scarf
add_torus("Scarf",(0,0,1.05),0.4,0.12,white)
# tentacles: 6 curved tubes via curves
import mathutils
for i in range(6):
    ang=i/6*2*math.pi
    bpy.ops.curve.primitive_bezier_curve_add(location=(math.cos(ang)*0.4, math.sin(ang)*0.4,0.9))
    c=bpy.context.active_object; c.name=f"Tent{i}"
    s=c.data.splines[0].bezier_points
    s[0].co=mathutils.Vector((0,0,0)); s[1].co=mathutils.Vector((math.cos(ang)*0.9, math.sin(ang)*0.9,-0.4))
    s[0].handle_left_type='AUTO'; s[0].handle_right_type='AUTO'; s[1].handle_left_type='AUTO'; s[1].handle_right_type='AUTO'
    c.data.bevel_depth=0.12
    c.data.materials.append(red)

# Booth counter
counter=prim_mesh("Counter",(0,1.8,0.55),(1.8,0.5,0.55),wood,'cube')
top=prim_mesh("CounterTop",(0,1.8,1.12),(1.9,0.6,0.06),darkwood,'cube')
# posts + roof
for x in (-1.8,1.8):
    prim_mesh(f"Post{x}",(x,1.8,1.8),(0.08,0.08,1.2),darkwood,'cube')
roof=prim_mesh("Roof",(0,1.8,3.0),(2.2,1.0,0.12),roofm,'cube')
# noren curtain: 3 planes
for i,xx in enumerate((-0.6,0,0.6)):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_plane_add(location=(xx,1.25,2.4))
    o=bpy.context.active_object; o.name=f"Noren{i}"; o.scale=(0.35,1,0.35)
    o.data.materials.append(cream if i!=1 else roofm)
# back wall / banner pole
prim_mesh("BackWall",(0,3.0,1.5),(2.0,0.1,1.5),cream,'cube')
# Ramen bowl on counter
add_cyl("Bowl",(0.8,1.8,1.35),0.32,0.22,white)
add_cyl("Broth",(0.8,1.8,1.42),0.27,0.05,broth)
add_torus("Narutomaki",(0.8,1.8,1.47),0.06,0.03,white)
for gx in (-0.1,0,0.1):
    add_cyl(f"Green{gx}",(0.8+gx,1.8+0.1,1.47),0.03,0.03,green)
# chopsticks
for dz in (0,0.06):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(location=(0.8,1.8,1.6),radius=0.015,depth=0.8)
    o=bpy.context.active_object; o.name=f"Stick{dz}"; o.location.z+=dz
    o.rotation_euler=(math.radians(90),0,math.radians(20))
    o.data.materials.append(darkwood)
# second bowl + lantern
add_uvsphere("Lantern",(-1.2,1.8,2.2),0.25,roofm,scale=(1,1,1.2))
# floor
prim_mesh("Floor",(0,1.0,0),(4,4,0.05),cream,'cube')

# camera + light
bpy.ops.object.camera_add(location=(4.5,-4.5,3.2))
cam=bpy.context.active_object
cam.rotation_euler=(math.radians(68),0,math.radians(45))
bpy.context.scene.camera=cam
bpy.ops.object.light_add(type='SUN',location=(3,-3,6))
bpy.context.scene.render.engine='BLENDER_WORKBENCH'
bpy.context.scene.render.resolution_x=800
bpy.context.scene.render.resolution_y=600
result={"ok":True}

import bpy, os
os.makedirs("output", exist_ok=True)
bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(filepath="output/octopus-chef.glb", export_format='GLB')
bpy.context.scene.render.filepath="output/render1.png"
bpy.context.scene.render.resolution_x=900; bpy.context.scene.render.resolution_y=700
bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)
# second angle
cam=bpy.context.scene.camera
cam.location=(-4.5,-4.0,2.8)
import math
cam.rotation_euler=(math.radians(70),0,math.radians(-45))
bpy.context.scene.render.filepath="output/render2.png"
bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)
result={"ok":True}

Made a stylized octopus chef at a ramen booth, built entirely in Blender with `bpy` primitives.

- `octopus-chef.glb` (~0.7 MB) — red octopus head with white eyes, white chef hat and scarf, six tube tentacles, behind a wooden booth with posts, red roof, cream back wall, noren curtain panels, paper lantern, counter with a ramen bowl (broth, narutomaki, greens, chopsticks), plus floor.
- `render1.png` — front view of the chef in the booth.
- `render2.png` — three-quarter side view.
